title: What is Epic Haiku?
text:
What is Epic Haiku?

Epic Haiku is a mobile application designed for healthcare providers, allowing them to access the Epic electronic health record (EHR) system from their smartphones or tablets. It enables convenient access to patient information, messaging, and schedule management on the go.

title: How do I download and install Epic Haiku?
text:
How do I download and install Epic Haiku?

Epic Haiku can be downloaded from the Apple App Store or Google Play Store. After installation, you'll need to configure the app with your organization's server settings, which can be obtained from your IT department.

title: What can I do with Epic Haiku?
text:
What can I do with Epic Haiku?

With Epic Haiku, you can:

- View patient charts, including lab results, medications, and medical history.

- Manage your schedule and review upcoming appointments.

- Communicate securely with other providers or care team members.

- Capture clinical photos and securely upload them to the patient’s record.

title: Is Epic Haiku secure?
text:
Is Epic Haiku secure?

Yes, Epic Haiku uses secure, encrypted connections to ensure that patient data is protected. It complies with HIPAA regulations to safeguard patient privacy.

title: Can I use Epic Haiku to prescribe medications?
text:
Can I use Epic Haiku to prescribe medications?

Epic Haiku allows you to view patient medications and make medication-related notes, but prescribing capabilities may vary depending on your organization's configuration. Check with your IT department for specific features available in your setup.

title: What devices are compatible with Epic Haiku?
text:
What devices are compatible with Epic Haiku?

Epic Haiku is compatible with iOS and Android devices. Ensure that your device is running a supported version of the operating system as specified in the app's requirements on the App Store or Google Play.

title: How do I troubleshoot issues with Epic Haiku?
text:
How do I troubleshoot issues with Epic Haiku?

If you encounter issues, first ensure that your app and device are updated to the latest versions. If problems persist, contact your IT support team for assistance with configuration or connectivity issues.

title: How do I log in to Epic Haiku?
text:
How do I log in to Epic Haiku?

You can log in to Epic Haiku using your standard Epic credentials. Ensure that your device is connected to the internet and that you have the necessary server information configured in the app.

title: Who should I contact for help with Epic Haiku?
text:
Who should I contact for help with Epic Haiku?

For any issues or questions related to Epic Haiku, contact your organization's IT support team. They can assist with installation, configuration, and troubleshooting.

title: Can I access Epic Haiku outside of my healthcare facility?
text:
Can I access Epic Haiku outside of my healthcare facility?

Yes, as long as you have an internet connection and the necessary security configurations in place, you can access Epic Haiku from anywhere.

title: Why did we change from aXium and what is Epic?
text:
Why did we change from aXium and what is Epic?

The change from aXium to Epic Wisdom was made to provide UT
Dentistry with a more secure, integrated and efficient electronic health record
system. Epic Wisdom offers a powerful and comprehensive platform that provides a
full health history for patients with existing medical records in Epic through
other care providers.

Epic is a leading provider of electronic health record
solutions used by healthcare organizations to manage patient information,
streamline workflows and improve outcomes. More information on Epic can be
found on their website.

Epic Wisdom makes it easier for our users to combine a
patient’s medical and dental history, including allergies, previous procedures,
medications, and more, in one location. It also improves collaboration and
communication between teams to facilitate secure and safe patient care
management.

The transition to Epic aligns UT Dentistry’s electronic health
record system with other UT Health San Antonio patient care groups. The update
coincides with the opening of the new Multispecialty and Research Hospital,
which will also use Epic.

title: Can patients pay their bills electronically on Epic?
text:
Can patients pay their bills electronically on Epic?

Patients can review previous bills and payments and see and
pay any outstanding balances electronically on Epic through the patient portal
(MyChart), allowing for convenient and secure payment options.

title: Why is Thrive training important?
text:
Why is Thrive training important?

According to the KLAS Arch Collaborative, clinicians who spend 3-5 hours a year on ongoing training are 2-3 times more satisfied with their EHR.1.
Thrive training helps clinicians establish good efficiency habits and tailor their workspaces to support their personal workflows. Users can apply the knowledge from Thrive training to their own work or use it to help educate others. Thrive training is hands-on and moves at a pace that encourages questions and participation, allowing clinicians to walk away from class ready to use what they learned the next time they log in to the system for patient care.

title: Who is the intended audience for Thrive training?
text:
Who is the intended audience for Thrive training?

Thrive classes are designed for clinicians who are using Epic in their day to day job. Thrive training is particularly impactful for clinicians who understand their core workflows but would like to increase their efficiency in the system. These users can be identified through self-selection or through efficiency data provided by tools like Signal, ASAP PEP, and NEAT.
Epic-led Thrive training is open to existing End-User Training Services (EUTS) organizations, as well as organizations who haven't yet used EUTS. If you are not already participating in EUTS, talk to your Epic representative to get started.

title: What about the existing patient information in axiUm?
text:
What about the existing patient information in axiUm?

Existing patient information from the last five years in aXium has been successfully migrated and integrated into Epic Wisdom, ensuring continuity of care and access to historical data and patient information. Clinics and users with previous aXium access will still be able to use aXium in read-only mode to retrieve historical data and information that was not migrated to Epic. Patients not seen for five years or more will be treated as new patients.

title: AI Text Assistant
text:
AI Text Assistant

Is currently being piloted by specific departments (will be available to all in the next upgrade, August 2026).
To more quickly write notes, patient instructions, letters, and In Basket messages, clinicians can use AI-powered text action tools to:
- Summarize a piece of text that the clinician wrote to make it shorter or update the formatting, such as turning a paragraph into a list.
- Update the text to make sense to a specific audience, such as translating clinical jargon into wording that a patient can more easily understand.

title: Abridge Dictation
text:
Abridge Dictation

Is currently being piloted by specific departments. Verbatim Mode allows clinicians to more easily create their ideal clinical note through any combination of summarized and verbatim, word-for-word content—captured before or after note generation.

title: Dashboard Insights
text:
Dashboard Insights

Sometimes it would be nice to have an assistant to help walk you through what all that data on your dashboard means. Generative AI tools summarize reporting content, suggest possible conclusions, and identify key insights.

title: Draft Hospital Course in Discharge Summary
text:
Draft Hospital Course in Discharge Summary

Reduce physicians' documentation load by using generative AI to draft a hospital course note using data already available in the patient's chart.

title: Inpatient Insights
text:
Inpatient Insights

Rounding clinicians see a complex mix of patients, ranging from those they've been checking in with every day to those they've never met before. To help them quickly prepare for each of those patients, they can use generative AI to create three types of insights to fit the type of information and level of detail that would be most helpful: 

- Patient Story insights are designed to familiarize clinicians with a patient they have not previously encountered. These summaries include history from notes and chart data, recent events, and other details related to the current admission, helping them prioritize and plan their care efficiently. Patient Story summaries are organized into three sections: history, events during admission, and recent events. The recent events section includes similar information to the freestanding Recent Events summary described below.

- Notes summaries focus on summarizing relevant details from recent notes on the patient, helping clinicians quickly get up to speed on recent observations and developments or see highlights from the rest of the treatment team. 

- Recent Events summaries provide an overview of recently documented information on the patient, including intake/output, medications, results, orders, the problem list, notes, vitals, nursing assessments, and code events, ensuring that clinicians are aware of significant recent changes in a patient's condition since the last time they rounded.

title: PB Coding Assistant
text:
PB Coding Assistant

Save coders time so they can process more sessions and focus on those that require more expertise, helping maximize reimbursements. The Coding Assistant shows coders a list of potential diagnosis and procedure codes they might want to add based on notes that are relevant to a particular charge session, helping them review charge sessions efficiently and avoid jumping between many activities in search of relevant information.

Qualifying notes are automatically processed behind the scenes before a coder reviews the session, and they can jump to the source of supporting documentation when they need additional context. Cited text is highlighted in the note so they can decide whether the suggestion makes sense, all without needing to access Chart Review. When they decide to use a potential code, they can quickly add, swap, or remove codes from the charge session directly.

title: InBasket Categorization
text:
InBasket Categorization

Is currently being piloted by specific departments. In Basket automatically categorizes patient-initiated messages into subjects like Clinical Advice, Paperwork, or Scheduling, using a predictive model to help care teams triage and prioritize incoming requests. This allows staff to filter messages based on their roles, reducing response times and improving efficiency in handling patient communications.

title: InBasket Urgency
text:
InBasket Urgency

Is currently being piloted by specific departments. The Potentially Urgent predictive model automatically assigns urgency levels to patient messages, helping clinicians prioritize responses to potentially urgent communications while managing increasing message volumes. Currently, it categorizes messages as urgent, routine, or low (for FYI messages), with the option for users to manually select high urgency when needed.

title: Outpatient Insights
text: Outpatient Insights leverages generative AI to create patient visit summaries 36 hours prior to appointments, allowing clinicians to save time on preparation and stay informed about past visits, including external notes from Care Everywhere. The system automatically updates summaries if there are changes to the patient's record and generates new ones for walk-in appointments. Clinicians can personalize their summaries by selecting specific notes or topics of focus and have access to citations for each point, enabling them to quickly reference relevant context.

title: ART: Augmented Response Technology
text:
ART: Augmented Response Technology

Is currently being piloted by specific departments. Draft by Art streamlines communication for clinicians and staff by leveraging generative AI to create draft responses to patient messages. The system analyzes incoming messages from patients along with pertinent patient information to anticipate how a clinician or staff member might reply. It then generates a draft response that can be easily modified before being sent to the patient.

title: Ambient Orders
text:
Ambient Orders

Ambient AI tools utilize passive listening technology to capture clinical encounters through discreet devices, employing natural language processing and machine learning to structure, code, and stage draft orders directly in the clinician's EHR system. This automation enhances efficiency, boosts patient engagement, reduces clinician burnout, and improves accuracy by minimizing manual data entry errors.

title: Abridge tab in Hypersapce
text:
Abridge tab in Hypersapce

Clinicians can access Abridge features directly within the Epic Hyperspace interface, enabling them to summarize clinical documentation in brief sentences or short paragraphs. This integration aims to alleviate the documentation burden and reduce clinician burnout, allowing healthcare providers to concentrate more on patient care.

Hello World Billing Notifications

For Hello World Billing's SMS notifications, it’s important to clarify the key information typically communicated to end users. Here’s a general overview:
Account Balance Information: SMS notifications can inform users about current balances, overdue amounts, or successful payments.
Due Date Reminders: Friendly reminders a few days before payment due dates to help users avoid late fees.
Payment Confirmation: Users receive confirmations for successful payments, providing assurance and record of the transaction.
Dispute Notifications: For any billing disputes or adjustments, an SMS may inform users of resolution statuses.
Support and Contact Information: SMS notifications often include details on how users can contact support for billing questions.
Opt-in/Opt-out Options: Users should have the ability to manage their SMS notifications preferences for billing information.

text:
Trusted Exchange Framework (TEFCA)

The Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement™, also known as TEFCA™, outlines a common set of principles, terms, and conditions to support the development of a Common Agreement that helps enable the nationwide exchange of electronic health information (EHI) across disparate health information networks (HINs). The TEFCA is designed to scale EHI exchange nationwide and help ensure that HINs, health care providers, health plans, individuals, and many more stakeholders have secure access to their electronic health information when and where it is needed.

title: Extract Sciences - Aura Integration
text:
Extract Sciences - Aura Integration

Aura brings the promise of precision medicine within reach for the entire Epic community. With Aura, you can collaborate with specialty diagnostic labs in a fraction of the time necessary to configure traditional interfaces. Connect to a single compendium of tests from each participating lab, then download purpose-built configuration packages to update your local Epic build. After that, providers can use their existing Epic workflows to send orders to and receive discrete results from any lab on the network.
Today, oncology end users noted that Natera, Caris, and Gaurdant were the most common specialty diagnostic labs being used. The core workflows for these tests are managed outside of Epic with results scanned and separate processes to share with patients via MyChart.
